children: Basis bids for soybeans and corn shipped by barge to the US Gulf Coast were steady to weaker on Thursday, as export buyers looked to South America for supplies and US grain and soy futures saw a choppy day of trading, traders said.

US soybean futures gained strength during the session from surging cash prices for soymeal, a feed ingredient, but also faced mounting pressure from a flurry of profit-taking and a setback in crude oil, analysts said.

Meanwhile, the run-up to next week's meeting between presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping kept attention on Chinese demand for US soy. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Tuesday that he plans to meet his Chinese counterpart He Lifeng this weekend, ahead of the leaders' meeting next week.

South Korean grain buyers have been making corn purchases this week from South America, traders said. Leading South Korean feedmaker Nonghyup Feed Inc. (NOFI) purchased around 68,000 metric tons of animal feed corn in a private deal on Thursday without an international tender being issued, European traders said. The corn was expected to be sourced from either South America or South Africa.

The Korea Feed Association (KFA) in South Korea purchased about 58,000 metric tons of animal feed corn expected to be sourced from South America or South Africa in a private deal on Thursday without issuing an international tender, European traders said.

The purchases were somewhat seasonally unexpected, one US trader said, as this tends to be the time of year when buyers are looking to the US market for supplies. But the recent rally in grains and oilseeds has had some exporters looking elsewhere for better deals, the trader said.
Freight values for empty barges remain elevated, with Gulf-area barge fleets starting to show signs of getting jammed up and delays building, barge sources said.

CIF soybean barges loaded in October traded at 97 cents over CBOT November soybean (SX26) futures, while barges loaded in December/January traded at 109 cents over CBOT January 2027 soybean (SF27) futures.
Meanwhile, CIF soybean barges loaded in September had no bids and offers turned lower, while barges loaded in October were steady — bid at 95 cents over CBOT November soybean (SX26) futures.
FOB export premiums for Gulf soybean shipments in October were steady, offered at around 124 cents over November futures, while November shipments were offered at 127 cents over futures.
Bids for CIF corn barges were lower, with September loadings unquoted but offers dropped 3 cents, while October barge bids eased 3 cents at 83 cents over CBOT December corn (CZ26) futures.

FOB export premiums for Gulf corn vessels loaded in the first half of October were also steady, offered at around 106 cents over December futures, while latter-half October were offered at 109 cents over December futures.
